root_cause.text: smb2_check_message() unconditionally returns success for SMB2_CREATE responses with STATUS_STOPPED_ON_SYMLINK without checking if the received packet length is at least sizeof(struct smb2_err_rsp), allowing an out-of-bounds read in symlink_data() when the buffer is smaller.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds `len > calc_len` to the condition in smb2_check_message(), and the CVE description explicitly states that "smb2_check_message() returns success without length validation for the symlink error response" and that accessing fields like err->ErrorContextCount when iov_len is smaller than sizeof(struct smb2_err_rsp) causes an out-of-bounds read.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix overly permissive length check for symlink create failures by requiring len > calc_len to avoid accepting malformed packets.
intent_record.what: Added the condition `len > calc_len` to an existing if statement that checks for SMB2_CREATE_HE command and STATUS_STOPPED_ON_SYMLINK status.
intent_record.how: The function now only returns 0 (accepting the length mismatch) when the actual packet length is strictly greater than the calculated length, rather than unconditionally accepting any mismatch for symlink create failures.

vuln_statements.stmt_text: if (le32_to_cpu(hdr->Status) == STATUS_STOPPED_ON_SYMLINK && hdr->Command == SMB2_CREATE && len > calc_len) {
vuln_statements.explanation: This conditional return bypasses proper length validation for SMB2_CREATE responses with STATUS_STOPPED_ON_SYMLINK. It does not ensure the received packet length is at least sizeof(struct smb2_err_rsp), leading to an out-of-bounds read in symlink_data() when the buffer is too small.
